title: Dispute Management Agents
description: Card dispute management with six sequential agents on Azure AI Foundry Hosted Agents, with mandatory human approval before irreversible actions.
problem: A dispute's lifecycle involves classification, evidence gathering, regulatory checks, communication and resolution. The chain automates all six steps but halts chargebacks and final closure behind an explicit human approval gate.

architecture.caption: Five layers: operations console, hosted agent in Foundry, six-agent chain, business integrations, and governance with data.

flow: The operator registers or reviews the claim in the operations console published on Azure Container Apps.
The case enters the Hosted Agent of the Foundry project, built with Agent Framework and published through ResponsesHostServer.
The chain runs sequentially: Intake classifies, Case builds the customer's 360° view and Data gathers transaction and merchant evidence.
Each agent queries business systems through function tools: CRM, card management, merchant data and the fraud engine.
Investigation checks the case against regulations via RAG and sets hitl_required if the fraud score exceeds 75, the amount exceeds USD 1,500 or confidence drops below 0.70.
Communication notifies the customer and handles provisional credit; Resolution executes the chargeback, both after human approval.

components.name: Container Registry
components.role: Private registry for the console image.

components.name: Azure Cosmos DB
components.role: State and traceability of processed cases.

insight.title: Human-in-the-Loop enforced by the platform
insight.text: The chargeback and final-resolution tools are declared with approval_mode="always_require": it is the Foundry runtime that pauses execution and demands approval. The guarantee does not depend on the prompt or on the model's discipline, but on the platform.
